Chip Industry Technical Paper Roundup: Sept. 29

6

A7 CFET vs. A10 NSFETs; wafer-scale sub-5nm MoS₂ transistors; multi-kW power delivery for 3D HI; copper microstructure and TSV residual stress; Rowhammer attacks on GPUs; gate-level RTL Trojan localization; concurrent HBM and host-memory access for LLM inference; agent-driven chip design using HLS.

September 29th, 2026 -

By: Linda Christensen

New technical papers recently added to Semiconductor Engineering’s library:

Technical Paper
Research Organizations

System-Technology Co-Evaluation of A7 CFET and A10 NSFET Technologies from Cell Parasitics to Chip Reliability
TU Munich, University of Modena and Reggio Emilia, Applied Materials

Wafer-scale 2D MoS₂ transistors with sub-5nm channel length and subthreshold performance beyond the silicon limit
Carnegie Mellon University, University of Florida, MIT, Texas A&M University

Toward Multi-kW Power Delivery Methodologies for Advanced 3D Heterogeneous Integration
University of Minnesota

Experimental Evidence for the Impact of Copper Microstructure on Residual Stress of Through Silicon Via
Purdue University, UCLA

GPUThor: Amplifying Rowhammer Attacks via Non-Uniform Patterns to Exploit ECC-Protected GPUs
University of Toronto

Demystifying Gate-Level Localization of RTL Trojans
University of Wisconsin–Madison, Marist University

BOOST: Concurrent Access to Host Memory and HBM to Accelerate LLM Inference
Georgia Tech, Nvidia Research, Stanford University

Can Agents Design Better Chips with a Higher Level Abstraction?
UCLA
